title: QR Print Studio
summary: Design readable QR tags and plant labels for 3D printing. Start with a URL or an existing QR image, add names, choose a stake or flat-tag shape, and export printable bodies. The hosted edition can also use the plant collection and batch label workflows. It is a design/export tool; your slicer or label-printer application still prepares and sends the print.
features: Generate from a link or decode PNG, JPG, WebP and PDF QR artwork.
Combine QR and names; rotate content and choose a centred stake, left/right flag or flat tag.
Adjust blade, neck and label dimensions and preview the resulting geometry.
Create two blades that slot together; export a small fit test before the full design.
Export 3MF or aligned STL bodies so the slicer can assign materials to the intended regions.
Search plants, retain per-plant settings and preview/export selected tags on multiple plates.
Set actual label-roll dimensions, padding, type size and printer resolution; export PDF or an Excel name batch.
workflows: Make your first QR tag
Paste an ordinary demonstration URL into the QR input. If importing artwork, choose a clear image or PDF and verify the decoded link before designing around it.
Enter a short readable name; add a scientific name only if useful. Choose a starting layout and tag type.
Set overall dimensions, label placement and content rotation. Refresh the preview and check that lettering, QR modules and margins remain distinct.
Export a colour 3MF, open it in your slicer and assign the intended filament colours. Verify size and part placement before slicing.
Print one test tag and scan the physical result. A successful model export does not demonstrate that your print is optically readable.
Choose the right shape
Use a flat tag for attachment to a surface, a centred stake for a straight insertion point, or a left/right flag when the label needs to sit beside the stake.
For slotted spikes, inspect both blades in the assembly preview, then export and print the fit-test STL.
Adjust the slot fit based on your printer and material. Only then export the full pair. Keep the two blades as their intended separate parts.
Batch plant tags — hosted edition
Open All plants, refresh the collection and search for the group you want. Select matching plants or individual records.
Open a plant’s Tag editor, refine its layout and save that plant’s print settings to NAS. Review the selected nozzle and name treatment.
Preview selected tags. Resolve crowded names or unsuitable sizes before exporting the multi-plate 3MF.
Open the batch in the slicer and review every plate, including purge-tower and edge clearances. Per-plant settings should not be assumed identical.
Make name stickers — hosted edition
Choose the label-printer mode. Enter the dimensions printed on your roll; length runs along the roll and height across it.
Adjust padding and letter size. The D11 layout respects its narrower printable width; text wrapping is preferable to unreadably shrinking every name.
Choose PDF when you need to retain the designed dimensions and layout, and print at actual size / 100%.
Choose the Excel batch for a printer application’s data import. Bind Plant name to a text field in that application. Excel supplies names; it does not preserve the PDF’s exact layout.
Name stickers contain text; the QR remains on the 3D-printed stake. Use the label-dimension option to reserve a matching flat space on the stake.
limits: A browser preview and valid 3MF archive have been checked. Physical printing, scanning and the full range of printers/materials remain separate checks. The standalone export has no connected plant catalog or NAS batch service.
